newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo claims Remeron superior to Prozac.
newsitem.headline: Akzo claims Remeron superior to Prozac.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Monday trials involving the antidepressant Remeron, made by its Organon unit, showed it to be more effective than Prozac.
"Results show that at weeks three and four, patients treated with Remeron were significantly less depressed than those taking (SSRI) Prozac," Akzo said in a statement.
The statement followed the first double-blind trial of the drug involving 120 patients in the Netherlands, UK and Belgium.
The results were presented at a European College of Neuropsychopharmacology congress in Amsterdam by Professor Stuart Montgomery from St Mary's Hospital in London.
He said the new results showed that "Remeron really ought to replace conventional antidepressants such as the tricyclics and SSRIs like Prozac in the treatment of depression."
Antidepressants come in three main classes -- tricyclics, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressants (NaSSAs).
Remeron is currently available in the Netherlands, United States, Germany, Finland, Denmark and Brazil and will be introduced in Sweden and Greece next month.
Sales of Eli Lilly's Prozac, the best-selling treatment for depression -- which conservatively affects some 340 million people worldwide -- were over $2 billion in 1995.
